text:
rachel: hey everyone, rachel here (platform eng). setting up CI to hit the hosted sandbox later today. 2 quick questions: 1) what's the safest way to create/revoke API keys for PR builds? 2) what's the conservative per-project sandbox quota so i can design retries?

devex: welcome rachel :wave: short answers: 1) use ephemeral keys for PRs; create per-run or per-branch with a 1-4h TTL and rotate. 2) defaults are pretty conservative (often ~50-100 reqs/min per project) but vary by org. always plan for 429s.

rachel: can ephemeral keys be created programmatically (via internal API) or only via Console? i want per-build automation.

infra-ops: you can use the internal key creation endpoint if your CI has a service account with the right perms. avoid giving that service account wide powers. if you expect >100 keys/hour, talk to infra firstwe can advise on batching.

security: if you automate key creation, constrain scopes and TTL, and rotate the service account credentials regularly. log auditing is enabled for key ops; also add a CI step to scrub any token-like strings from logs/artifacts.

rachel: noted. about rate limits: i'm planning ~30 rps for 3 minutes from a single runner; each response ~350 tokens. should i request a temporary bump?

devex: 30 rps short burst usually OK, but because token output amplifies load, file a quota request if you want headroom. use Console -> Usage -> Quota Requests and include project id, start/end, target rps, and CIDR if you want IP whitelisting.

infra-ops: for the request, we need project id and the exact UTC window. we can approve short windows (up to a few hours) quickly. also: sandbox limits are enforced per-project by default. if your CI shares project id with other teams, mention that in the form.

rachel: what's the recommended backoff strategy for CI so tests don't flake noisily?

devex: exponential backoff with full jitter is standard. honor Retry-After header when present and fail fast for tests that assert correctness. for non-critical smoke tests, retry a few times then mark flaky.

infra-ops: also set a hard per-call timeout and cap max_tokens in the request to keep response sizes predictable. example curl payload we use for smoke tests:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"open-redwood-1-small","input":"smoke","max_tokens":350}'
```

rachel: thanks. can infra allowlist our CI runner IP for the test window? that would help debugging.

infra-ops: yes, include CIDR in the quota request and we'll add a short-lived allowlist entry. note: allowlist doesn't bypass quota limits entirely; it helps with networking and some rate policies.

onboarding-bot: reminder: new-hires checklist item "Create ephemeral sandbox key" assigned to @rachel is pending.

rachel: submitted request for project: platform-sandbox (window 1771507200-1771510800 UTC, target 120 rps, CIDR 203.0.113.0/32). created ephemeral key expiring in 3h and updated CI secret store. thanks all!

devex: i'll attach a short-term alert to that project and monitor for 429 spikes during the window. ping here if you want us to escalate.

security: one last reminder: add a log-scrub step and don't include keys in artifacts. ephemeral keys reduce risk if something leaks.

rachel: will do, appreciate the quick help :heart:
